questions.question: How many identical placards must be placed on a vehicle transporting hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: When refueling a vehicle transporting hazardous materials, what should you do?

options.text: Have someone other than the driver refuel.

questions.explanation: Always turn off the engine before refueling. Someone must always watch the nozzle while fuel is flowing.

questions.question: If a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, how should the hazardous materials be marked?

options.text: Circled by a pen or marker.

questions.explanation: Hazardous materials on a mixed shipping paper must be distinguished. They can be listed first, highlighted in a contrasting color, or marked with an "X" in the "HM" column.

questions.question: When a shipping paper has both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, how should hazardous materials be marked?

options.text: Circled by a pen or marker.
Written the same way as non-hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: One way to identify hazardous materials on a mixed shipping paper is to highlight them in a contrasting color.

questions.question: Besides reading the manual, what is the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials?

options.text: Talk to other hazardous materials drivers.

questions.explanation: The manual is the first step. You should also read federal and state rules about hazardous materials transportation and attend hazardous materials training courses.

questions.question: If cargo containing hazardous materials is leaking, what should the driver do?

options.text: Drive to find a phone to alert emergency personnel.
Drive to a hazardous materials cleanup facility.
Park the vehicle and contact emergency personnel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park the vehicle and contact emergency personnel.
questions.explanation: Stop driving as soon as it is safe. Continuing to drive spreads contamination. Park the vehicle, secure the area, stay with the vehicle, and get help.

questions.question: How often must hazardous materials employees be trained?

options.text: At least once every three years.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least once every three years.
questions.explanation: Employees who work with hazardous materials must be trained and tested at least once every three years.

questions.question: When transporting hazardous materials, where should placards be placed?

options.text: On all four sides of the vehicle.
Only for Class A licensed drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all four sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: What must emergency response information from the shipper include?
questions.explanation: Emergency response information must include: material descriptions and technical names; health hazards; fire or explosion risks; accident precautions; fire handling methods; spill or leak handling methods; and first aid measures.

questions.question: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on the shipping paper, which placard must you display?

options.text: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard.
questions.explanation: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on the shipping paper or package, display the "Poison Inhalation Hazard" or "Poison Gas" placard as appropriate.

questions.question: If your engine runs a pump for compressed gas delivery, when should you turn off the engine?
questions.explanation: Turn off your engine before unhooking the hoses when loading or unloading a compressed gas tank, even if your engine runs the pump for product transfer.

questions.question: What are used to warn others about hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped placards are placed on bulk packages and vehicles to warn others about hazardous materials. The shipper places them, and the driver must check that they are correct.

questions.question: How must containers of hazardous materials be secured?

options.text: They must be braced to prevent movement during transportation.
They must be made of cardboard.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must be braced to prevent movement during transportation.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials containers must be braced so they will not fall, slide, or bounce around during transport.

questions.question: What is the symbol for a marine pollutant?

options.text: A yellow triangle with an X through waves
A fish in a white triangle with an X through it
A light blue square with a dark blue X
A bird in a red octagon

questions.correctAnswerText: A fish in a white triangle with an X through it
questions.explanation: The marine pollutant symbol is a fish in a white triangle with an X through it.

questions.question: What must a shipping paper generally list?

options.text: The location of fire departments along the planned route.

questions.explanation: Shippers must list an emergency response telephone number on hazardous materials shipping papers. There are some exceptions to this rule.

questions.question: What is a Class 7 hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Radioactive materials are classified as Class 7 hazardous materials.

questions.question: Where should shipping papers be kept?

options.text: Easily seen by anyone entering the cab

questions.correctAnswerText: Easily seen by anyone entering the cab
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's door or another location where you can easily reach them while wearing your seat belt. They must be clearly visible to anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: Hazardous materials regulations are intended to protect all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials regulations exist to protect the driver, others near the vehicle, and the environment. Buildings are not the primary focus of these regulations.

questions.question: What should you do if a hazardous materials label does not fit on a package?

options.text: Place the label on a tag securely attached to the package
Attach a QR code to be scanned
Reduce the size of the label to fit it on the package

questions.correctAnswerText: Place the label on a tag securely attached to the package
questions.explanation: If a hazard label will not fit completely on a package, place it on a tag that is securely attached to the package.

questions.question: What does a driver need to accept a hazardous materials package, unless it is clearly unsafe?
questions.explanation: Unless a package is clearly unsafe or does not follow Hazardous Materials Regulations, you can accept the shipper's certification that it was properly packaged.

questions.question: Where should hazardous materials shipping papers be kept?

options.text: In a pouch attached to the driver's side door.
Taped to the passenger's side window.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a pouch attached to the driver's side door.
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's side door or in a place the driver can easily reach while wearing a seat belt. Papers must be easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: What sign might show that a shipment contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
The cargo is picked up from a supermarket.
The cargo is in cardboard boxes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Cylinders and drums often hold hazardous materials. Take proper precautions when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.question: How far away must a person stay from a vehicle with Class 3 or Division 2.1 materials before smoking?
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a cargo tank carrying Class 3 or Division 2.1 hazardous materials.

questions.question: What is required when transporting explosives?

options.text: You must have a written route plan.
You should take the shortest possible route.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must have a written route plan.
questions.explanation: You must follow a written route plan when carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives. Avoid busy areas, crowds, tunnels, narrow streets, and alleys. Check for any route restrictions before you drive.

questions.question: What should you do if flammable liquids must be moved to another tank?

options.text: You may transfer them on the road as long as no one is nearby.
Do not transfer them on a public road unless it is an emergency.
Keep the transfer secret when moving to another tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not transfer them on a public road unless it is an emergency.
questions.explanation: Never transfer flammable liquids from one vehicle to another on a public road unless it is an emergency. Always warn others about the hazards of the materials.

questions.question: What does a driver need to accept a package of hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The shipper certifies that hazardous materials are packaged correctly. You may accept the package unless it looks unsafe or does not follow the rules. Trust the shipper's certification if the package looks safe.

questions.question: What material should a floor liner be made of when transporting Division 1.3 materials?
questions.explanation: Use a floor liner when transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 materials. The floor must be tight. The liner must be non-metallic or non-ferrous metal. Non-ferrous metals contain no iron.

questions.question: What is the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials besides reading the manual?
questions.explanation: The manual has information for the written test, but not all safety information. Hazardous materials training courses teach you how to do the job safely.

questions.question: Which type of material requires a transport index?
questions.explanation: Some radioactive materials need a transport index. This number shows how much control is needed during transport. The total transport index for all cargo in one vehicle cannot be more than 50.

questions.question: How many classes of hazardous materials are there?
questions.explanation: There are nine hazardous materials classes. Each class shows the risks of that type of material.
